claims.claim: Version 1.08a takes the Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition as one of its two foundations.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a
claims.quote: The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th edition

claims.claim: The earlier version 1.04a of the same guide took the Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition as its foundation, so the house authority moved one Chicago edition between the two releases.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.04a
claims.quote: The Chicago Manual of Style, 16th edition

claims.claim: The superseded version of the guide is numbered 1.04a and carries a 2013 copyright line.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.04a

claims.claim: Neither released version of the D&D style guide names an author, editor or compiler anywhere in its pages; the only attribution is the corporate copyright line.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a (11 pages) and v1.04a (9 pages)

claims.claim: The house style guide states that in rules text the D&D editors prefer to achieve gender neutrality by writing in the second person wherever possible.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Achieving Gender Neutrality
claims.quote: neutrality by writing in the second person

claims.claim: The house style guide instructs writers to avoid page references as much as possible.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Page References
claims.quote: We avoid page references as much as possible.

claims.claim: The guide's stated reason for avoiding page references is that they are labor-intensive, having to be added by hand during galley review.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Page References
claims.quote: They are labor-intensive (they must be added by

claims.claim: The guide tells writers to use cross-references judiciously because they are easily overused.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Cross-References

claims.claim: The guide sets a monster's name in bold only on its first appearance in an encounter area or subsection, not on every mention.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Terms to Set in Bold
claims.quote: Set a monster’s name in bold only the first time

claims.claim: The guide forbids any word coming between the number of monsters appearing and the name of the stat block.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Terms to Set in Bold
claims.quote: Make sure no text gets between the number of

claims.claim: The guide treats italicized spell and magic item names as titles rather than as descriptions of the thing they create.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing v1.08a, Terms to Italicize
claims.quote: The italicized terms are treated as titles

claims.claim: Ray Vallese, the Planescape line's editor, says the products were often written in a wry, overly clever voice that smirked at the setting's ignorant outsiders.
claims.source: Ray Vallese, TSR Planescape editor, interviewed at Exposition Break, 2022
claims.quote: written in a wry, overly clever voice that smirked

claims.claim: Monte Cook recalls that WotC president Peter Adkison did not want a line whose characters used slang he could not understand to discuss philosophy.
claims.source: Monte Cook, Planescape designer, interviewed at Exposition Break, 2022
claims.quote: not people using slang he didn’t understand to discuss philosophy
claims.page: answer on Planescape after the WotC purchase

claims.claim: Christopher Perkins states as a working practice that he keeps his descriptions spare.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, The Dungeon Master Experience: T'wit, Dungeon 197, 2011

claims.claim: Perkins says he keeps his NPC descriptions brief as well.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, The Dungeon Master Experience: T'wit, Dungeon 197, 2011
claims.quote: I keep my NPC descriptions brief as well.
